messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance identification for categorical variables
parts:
Try 

cat1[[1]] # for the configural invariance model
cat1[[2]] # for the weak invariance model
cat1[[3]] # for the strong invariance model

On Sat, May 21, 2016 at 12:15 AM, Margarita Olivera <margari...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am examining measurement invariance for categorical variables.
I want to use Millsap and Tein (2004) identification constraints in which:
- the factor loading for the reference item is fixed to cero
- one threshold for the reference item is fixed to cero
- one threshold for each item is fixed to equality across groups,
- the mean of the latent factor is fixed to cero in one group and free in the other.

I ran the configural model but it looks like some other identification constraints are being used. The thresholds are not fixed across groups and the latent variable mean is fixed to cero in both groups. 

This is my syntax. 
Caregivers.conf <- cfa(Fmod1, data=female, ordered= c("fc1","fc4","fc5","fc6","fc9"),
                       parameterization = "theta",
                       group = "aslang") 
summary(Caregivers.conf, fit.measures=T)


How can I override the defaults and use the ones suggested by Millsap and Tein?

I also tried:

cat1 <- measurementInvarianceCat(Fmod1,
                         data=female, 
                         ordered= c("fc1","fc4","fc5","fc6","fc9"),
                         parameterization = "theta",
                         group = "aslang",
                         std.lv = F, 
                         strict = F)

In this case I don't know how to get the parameter estimates for each model.

Thanks!
Margarita
